{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Fewer barriers to a first sale within 90 days. A sells B2B to developer-tool companies with a standard ToS/SLA and a GDPR privacy review. B must build verifiable parental consent under COPPA, plus unspecified state children's-privacy obligations, before it can collect any data from users under 13. That cuts into a six-week build and adds legal risk.",
    "A's demand evidence points at a buyer who already pays. The r/SaaS thread on the leader charging $399/month, and Statuspage's split billing running to $1,499+/mo, show the buyer already spends money and resents the price. B's strongest quote is a parent explaining why they chose not to pay $500/month, which is evidence of price resistance as much as demand.",
    "A has a sourced example of a solo operator succeeding in the category: Instatus at roughly $10k MRR. B cites no comparable solo outcome, and its cited competitors are either free (Khan Academy Kids, Samio) or drew public backlash (Mentava).",
    "A's buyers are reachable through channels a solo builder already uses (Indie Hackers, Product Hunt, dev SEO), and the brief gives organic SaaS CAC (~$205). B's only sourced channel is paid mobile installs at $2.50–$5.00 CPI in North America, which the brief itself calls hard to justify at under $15/month. Its organic channel is marked [unsourced cost], so it counts as missing.",
    "B's own case against says trust in children's products builds 'over months, not a six-week sales cycle'. Combined with heavy efficacy scrutiny in parent communities, this works directly against the 90-day goal. A's buyer can adopt a low-stakes, cheap tool quickly."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's case for low-cost distribution rests on organic parenting communities (r/daddit, r/homeschool, r/Parenting). The brief marks this channel's cost [unsourced] and admits reach and conversion are unproven, so under the rules it counts as missing. That leaves B with only the paid-install channel, which its own brief calls uneconomic. The '$25–$120/hour tutoring' figure supporting willingness to pay is also cited only as 'multiple tutoring-cost sources' with no link.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A wins mainly because B carries heavier structural obstacles: COPPA, the trust timeline, and paid-install economics. A's own evidence is not strong. It is selling against OneUptime's free tier and StillOnline's $9 plan, its SEO wedge is already occupied by Hyperping, its Product Hunt channel reportedly needs an existing audience, and Instatus's slow growth (~$500/mo MRR) suggests modest economics. The 90-day goal favors A because its first customer is more reachable, not because A has proven differentiation."
}
